definition: Hyperbole is deliberate exaggeration so extreme that no one is meant to take it literally.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word hyperbole. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know hyperbole should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Sports radio runs on hyperbole: every August, at least one caller declares the rookie 'the greatest athlete the species has produced.'

A stretch is far milder than hyperbole: calling a good chili 'the best in the county' pushes the truth a notch and still hopes to be believed, while hyperbole vaults past belief on purpose — 'this chili could power the grid.'
A tall tale goes beyond hyperbole: hyperbole is one impossible flourish inside ordinary talk, while a tall tale chains flourish to flourish into a whole story and dares the listener to object.

An overstatement pushes a claim past the facts while still asking to be believed — the home ground of overstated, taught in this same unit. Hyperbole blows the claim up so far that belief is never the point; the listener is meant to see through it.

Hype is promotional inflation — relentless talking-up designed to sell tickets, products, or candidates, and it wants to be believed. Hyperbole is a figure of speech: one spectacular impossibility, offered as flavor rather than fact.
